key_insight: Probability-based rewards in verifier-free RL can become nearly indistinguishable on long reasoning traces because of posterior concentration, making optimization unstable and inefficient.
engineering_relevance: For practical LLM training, RLCPR improves token efficiency and stabilizes reward learning by filtering concentration-prone samples and penalizing unnecessary trace length.
method: Uncertainty-aware data sampling to reduce concentration-prone rollouts before generation
Concentration-aware regularization to penalize overly long traces when posterior rewards collapse
Designed as a verifier-free RL framework compatible with GRPO-style optimization
evidence_signal: Experiments on seven benchmarks show RLCPR improves over the strongest verifier-free RL baseline by up to 4.0% and uses fewer tokens.
watch_item: Performance depends on detecting reward concentration reliably; if posterior collapse is misestimated, the regularization may suppress useful long reasoning traces.
paper_title: Rethinking Probability-Based Reinforcement Learning From Posterior Concentration
